text_fidelity_a:
TISUR Titanium Key Rings for Keychains, Quick Release Side Pushing Key Organizer Kit, Wisely Group Your Keys I like the way these rings work - you don't have to use fingernails or overcome a lot of tension to open the ring, and using them doesn't scratch them up or wear off the finish and create shiny spots. They seem resistant to being bent out of shape too...and all while being pleasantly lightweight. They're just...Keyring 2.0. A far superior alternative to the keyring model we've been struggling with for decades now.

Update: Yes, being titanium, they are indeed resistant to being bent out of shape. We have a little devil dog who likes to destroy things; I think it gives him a sense of agency. :) And one of the things he discovered he likes to do is pull the tags off his and his sister-dog's collars. The thin wire rings we originally used to attach the tags to collars made this easy for our destroyer-dog - he just pulled, and the wire rings would bend to allow him to pull the tags right off. I replaced those wire rings with TISUR titanium ones; they're nice and lightweight for the doggles' comfort, and our mechanically-inclined beast hasn't managed to pull a tag off either collar since.

I never thought there could be so much to say about something so simple as a keyring, but these really are next-level - an evolutionary stage beyond the classic keyring we've all used since I was a kid. Highly recommended for strength, light weight, and ease-of-use, all of which surpass the old design by a long shot.
text_fidelity_b: TISUR Titanium Key Rings for Keychains, Quick Release Side Pushing Key Organizer Kit, Wisely Group Your Keys

text_fidelity_a:
IRONMAN Exerpeutic 250 Manual Treadmill UPDATE Feb. 2016
I've changed my rating to 1 star. I think I was able to use this a total of 4 or 5 times before it died. You can see some of my experiences below in the original review. That creaking got louder, so I added a bit of WD40 into the roller (not the belt), which seemed to have solved the problem. Then at the end of last week, I was walking on it, and the thing suddenly froze up completely. Rollers won't move, belt won't move, nothing. It is DEAD.

To be fair, Paradigm (the manufacturer) did offer to replace the thing for me. But they had never even heard of this happening; I had no confidence that they really knew the product that well. If they replaced it, I'd have to pay for assembly AGAIN, and have no guarantee that the new machine wouldn't have the same problems. So we decided not to replace it with an Exerpeutic machine but go with a different brand entirely, and purchased from a local store that will give us support.

My original review:

I vascillated between giving this 3 or 4 stars. I like it, but am unsure about how long it will last. Firstly, we paid for the professional assembly and I'm glad we did because it took him over an hour to put it together. The packaging was poor, as other reviewers have said, and a couple of pieces were broken. One seemed to be a plastic bit that wasn't serving any purpose, so we cut it off with some tools.

In terms of workout, I like it quite a bit. Yes, the incline is fairly steep, but that's why I appreciate it; it's helps me break a sweat easily. The advantage of a manual is that you can speed up or slow down on your own time; you don't have to fiddle with buttons.

In terms of noise, it's louder than other Exerpeutic exercise equipment. In addition to the constant swishing sound, the treadmill creaks a fair amount. I'm hoping our downstairs neighbors won't be bothered (so far they haven't complained...we'll see). The creaking certainly doesn't instill confidence in the longevity of the product. But for the time being it's working and I'm grateful because we have a small apartment and could never fit a full-sized treadmill in here.
text_fidelity_b: IRONMAN Exerpeutic 250 Manual Treadmill

In the end we are thrilled to have this - it’ll be mine - and while I’m feeling like I’m not worthy (yet) of having it, I can’t wait to learn with it and get into this fun and rapidly growing game. For the amount and type of running that I do, the AiRunTech hydration running belt is perfect, and I suspect it also works great for the really long-distance runners.

Some features I found really useful:
- The combination of velcro adjustment plus a partially elastic band allowed me to fit the running belt exactly how I wanted it. After it's set, a buckle let's me get the belt on and off very quickly.
- The 10-oz water bottles fit securely in the belt and on my hips. The curved shape of the bottles align with the body contour better than straight bottles. An extra elastic loop makes sure each bottle stays in place and doesn't bounce.

Additional features I didn't use:
- Earphone outlet (I use bluetooth earphones)
- Energy gel loops (the distances I run are not long enough to need energy gel)

The photos on the Amazon description page show the runners wearing the belt with the pockets and water bottles on the front part of their bodies. Instead, I've worn it with the pocket and bottles on my back, and then I barely notice I am wearing the belt with its bottles.

text_fidelity_a:
Zippo Hand Warmer 2011 I have tried Penguin before Zippo.
I was pretty disappointed by Penguin, so I had high hope for Zippo. It's a cheap knock off of Hakukin(Peacock) hand warmer just like Penguin.
Zippo hand warmer is made in Taiwan, where as Hakukin(Peacock) is made in Japan by Hakukin for 80 years.
First imperssion of Zippo, looks just as cheap as Penguin(I think it was labeled as made in China). The burner looks different from Penguin or Hakukin.
I believe some of the positive reviews in here are real but I'm guessing there is a big quality control problem. Even if it starts working good, I don't think it'll keep working for a long time. Not too many follow up updates about positive experiences have been posted.
My first try, it got warmed up a little then kept the luke warmth for a while. It died and became cold before long. Second try, no luck.
Next, I'll try drop of fuel on the burner method which worked for Penguin a couple of times. It's the last resort which will ruin the burner something you shouldn't be doing.
I have to wonder why Hakukin is not sold in US? It seems to be available in England, why not in US? I would pay twice the price I paid for Zippo and still be happy with Hakukin.

*Update*(12-20-11)
There seems to be some organized effort by either the maker or the stores that sell them to rate down the negative reviews. Just look at the number of "Helpful".
Shameless.

*Update* (1-27-14)
Hakkin (Peacock) works!!!
I got it from -Bay through a vendor in Korea, even though it is starting to appear in amazon but the price is higher compare to -Bay. I was fully prepared to get disappointed because of the past experience with other products. It lighted the first time I tried, I couldn't believe it!! The catalyst(burner) even glows red in the dark that was something I wasn't expecting. I was like "Aha! This is how it supposed to work!!"
You pay more for the real thing but it's worth it. If it doesn't work, it's worthless no matter how much you save.
Get Hakkin, you won't regret it.
You will regret with Zippo.
text_fidelity_b: Zippo Hand Warmer 2011

STYLE: I have a large head (7 3/8), so unstructured hats look much better on me than taller sitting hats. That said, this hat is extremely unstructured, by nature, and is not going to win any fashion awards for most head shapes. It's got a distinct "this has a very specific function" style.

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier This thing is totally awesome. I was actually unaware that such fishing rod carriers existed. And of course, I barely had to browse other models to tell Thule would be a top contender.

Construction is fantastic. Rigid metal tubes and hardened plastic casing make "vault" an acceptable term for this.

One thing I didn't realize was that with this one (unlike the tackle fishing carriers), the length is not adjustable. The tubing is the same diameter for the entire length, so the two 5' sections connect in the middle with a compression connector tightened by hex screws. Because of this, you probably need to lock both parts of this to your rooftop rack, which leads to me locking...

...Locking this up is probably the weak point for me. This is unfortunate, because I always want better locking on any device, but this one isn't even as good as I might expect out of Thule. For one thing, it doesn't have the "one key" feature that Thule started using at some point (but you had to special order your device with your key type already if you wanted to go with that, so maybe consumers were too lazy to do it and the company gave up on it...not sure). Worse, though - and a real concern - is that this and my tackle vault use the same key, which leads me to wonder if I am able to open up and steal from any Thule rodvault I see out there in the wild? (Of course, I'd like to believe that anyone with enough money to buy a rodvault would be unlikely to steal fishing stuff from another person, but who knows...). Also, you need padlocks to lock the vault to the rack, which isn't that big of a deal, but I've seen other equipment with integrated locks that used the same key as the rest of the equipment, so it could be better.

This is big and heavy. More so than I expected. That adds some sense of value to it, but it also has me rethinking my storage place, especially considering its 10' permanent length unless I want to disassemble it with every use.

I'm also curious if this would hold some deep sea poles. I think so, but don't have any yet to try for myself.

In conclusion, it's hard to not be impressed with this thing, and yet I see some areas for improvement, mostly in the locking scheme. It is hard not to give this a full five stars simply because of its excellent sturdiness and bringing a whole new excellent way to transport large, expensive poles with even a small car, and without having to worry about them at all, for the most part.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Rodvault Fly Fishing Rod Carrier

text_fidelity_a:
Loowoko 50L Hiking Backpack, Waterproof Camping Essentials Bag with Rain Cover, 45+5 Liter Lightweight Backpacking Back Pack Some things I get stay in the box or bag and are used once in a while, but this backpack was opened, disappeared and months later, I was able to snag it from my ever traveling daughter. Let's see how it fared.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
First of all, my daughter is one of our kids who travels a LOT. She not only camps and hikes, but she also watches homes, is on the move constantly and needs an overnight bag that will fit all she needs for impromptu house sitting or overnights which she often has.

This backpack has a LOT of room in it. I am going to break it down section by section.

FRONT OF BAG
ZIPPERED POCKET
On the front of the bag is a zipper pocket with a fantastic covered zipper that keeps dry from wetness. It has room for emergency or every day supplies that you might need on the trail or on the go. It is where my daughter keeps bandaids, pads, nail clippers, tissue packets, and anything else that she might need to grab quickly.

DOUBLE SIDED ZIPPER POUCH
This is almost the shape of a cosmetic bag. It has two zipper heads so you can close it entirely by bringing both zippers to the one end, or move them both to the upper center for easy access to part of the pocket at once. This is very spacious to carry anything from elastic cords/stays and tent pegs, to cosmetics if this is used for traveling.

LOOPS
There are two sized loops on the bottom corners which allow for stakes, poles, umbrella, or other long items that you want to carry on a hike or while traveling. They will be even with the ground when placing the backpack down, so you have to keep that in mind.

SIDES
The sides of this backpack have plenty of room in them.

MESH POCKETS
Closed with an elastic band on each side, these pockets are perfect for water bottles, drink holders, small propane tanks (if you have a tiny camp stove), and other things. There are adjustable bands on each side of the backpack so that you can put talll items in the pockets too and they will be held into place on the sides.

TOP
There is a drawstring on the top of this backpack that allows the top to be shut before hooking the cap into place.

CAP
The cap on the top has a large zippered compartment perfect for inflatable pillow (deflated), emergency socks for quick change, or other items that you might need to have while on the trail. It also is a great place for dirty laundry when traveling if not hiking. It keeps it separate from the rest of the bag and you can keep a zipper plastic bag in there to isolate the dirt/smell.

CLIP
The cap has elastic inside it and clips into place, allowing for adjustments to items that might be in the backpack which are taller.

TOP OF CAP
There are two adjustable bands on the top of the cap which are perfect for a tent or bedroll or anything that you want to pack on there which won't be a problem to carry up near the upper back/neck area.

PART UP AGAINST BACK AND SIDE CLOSURES
This is the best part. There are two heavy pads which cushion the back when carrying this backpack on the shoulders.

HANGING LOOP
There is a hanging loop to hang this from a hook or tree.

STRAPS
There are other adjustable straps which allow for another tent/bedroll type item or sheets if you happen to be traveling and want to roll them up to travel with on nice days or a waterproof tent or other item if you are traveling in rain or snow.

STRAPS
The straps are adjustable and very comfortable. The padding is sufficient to keep this from digging into the shoulders too much.

SIDE BELTS
There is a belt which clips in the front when wearing this backpack. On each arm of the belt there are lined waterproof pouches which are similar to a small fanny pack. You can put jacknife, phone, keys, pen, lighter, matches, etc, and other items you might need on the trail. It is also fantastic for traveling as it fits a lot of small items you might want quick access to while on the road.

INSIDE
The inside is rather cavernous so you have freedom to put what you want inside. There is one very deep pocket up against where the back will be while wearing this and it will keep something flat in place.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Well, my daughter has been using this for MONTHS and I had a terrible time pining her down to make her give it back to me so I could write this review. She LOVES this thing. It is the best luggage for traveling and house sitting or pet sitting that you could imagine. She also brought it on two camping trips and although they did not get downpours, it was water resistant to a mild rain storm.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a very well set up backpack. It is perfect for hiking when you need to carry everything on your back and be as economical as possible with space. It is comfortable to wear, easy to access for small items and allows for small tent, camping bed, bedroll, and other items essential for camping. For traveling it allows for anything she could want to take with her quickly when having to stay for a few days somewhere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a fantastic backpack. I am very impressed at how efficient the features are, how well thought out this is, and how nicely made it is as well. I would definitely buy it again, because I know as soon as I hit enter, this will be snatched out of my hands once again, perhaps not to b seen again!
text_fidelity_b: Loowoko 50L Hiking Backpack, Waterproof Camping Essentials Bag with Rain Cover, 45+5 Liter Lightweight Backpacking Back Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Wayfarer Adult Bike Hybrid Retro-Styled Cruiser, Step-Over or Step-Through Frame Option, 7-Speed Drivetrain, Rear Rack, 700C Wheels, Multiple Colors This is a very good bike for the price. Some people are like 'oh it took only a few hours to put together', but I am a student who has a flexible schedule and I can say it took longer than a few hours. The initial assembly took a few hours - around 4 - but the tweaking took a few days. When I first put it together I felt glorious - like I had finished building a colosseum. I decide to take this work of art out for a spin at 11pm. Once I get outside, I get onto the sidewalk and prepare for take off. I mount the bike and immediately take a dive as both the seat and handle bar give in. It was painful.. for my ego. So I go back inside and tinker away. Then come out and hooray, the seat is kind of stable, but the handlebar is shaky. I throw caution to the wind and start riding.. or peddling.. then I see that the chain is like not in place or something? I'm not a mechanic. But I use some of the wisdom my father passed on to me to fix the chain (align it with the gear.. it was not hard or complicated lol.. but if you're not expecting it, then you feel like a fool).. anyway, I am telling you all of this so that when you buy this awesome bike, you won't feel disheartened by the fact that it might not take a minute to put together. Also, don't go to a repair person until you just need it to be tightened.. because you'll have a much better experience if you know why your bike messes up and how to fix it easily when it does. I ended up going to get it tightened because the seat and handlebar war just not tightening with my arm. So the guy who did it also gave my bike a check up and totally validated my pride by saying I did a great job. He only charged $5 for labor (but others did the same for free). Another bike repair man filled my bike with air and also adjusted the seat for me, since I had it a bit high. A lot of people will give you advice on how to sit on your bike, but don't change all the time. Test it out, and if it feels weird and to laborious then go back. Sometimes the advice is for efficiency, but a lot of times it given by veteran bikers who found their way after years of biking.
anyway, good luck.

These are not specifically cold weather gloves but they're acceptable protection from the cold. So far I'm happy with them.

The main issue I have with most gloves is finding gloves that fit me properly. I have huge hands so often gloves that are made for large or extra-large hands still don't quite fit. I selected the extra-large size and these actually fit me, though they are slightly snug. They do not feel strained when I wear them and ball my fist, nor do they feel constricting. That's a huge plus for me.

These are more substantial than typical gloves that one would wear for warmth. They're reinforced at the knuckles and are made to stretch under strain. These will work for weightlifting, though I probably would opt for something a little more substantial still in that specific context (that's just me).

Working with the camera these don't get in the way or slow me down, and that's really my main concern. They keep my hands warm enough to matter while my fingers are exposed enough to work the camera controls.

I like these gloves and expect to get many seasons of use from them. They're comfortable, they fit me properly and they work in the context for which I got them without getting in the way.

text_fidelity_a:
Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game USA Stars and Stripes: 2 Regulation MDF Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, 2 x 3 Foot One game that seems to be quite popular nowadays is cornhole. It’s a simple game and I often find it at local taverns, breweries, etc that have a large outdoor space. It’s also the type of game I find at friend’s houses and so it made sense to get a set of my own, the Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set.

With the American flag design on the two cornhole boards, this set has a patriotic look, which adds to its appeal, since it is certainly better than the plain cornhole boards so common in backyards across America. The boards come complete with bean bags, too, but there is no net to catch the bags, like with some cornhole sets. With this set, the bags will go through the opening and hit the surface beneath, so you need to make sure to place the boards on a reasonably clean surface.

The wood construction of this cornhole set is nice and I like how they attach together with Velcro. There are Velcro strips on the backs of the boards and this makes it easier to carry the boards around. The Velcro keeps them together, so when it comes time to pack up and leave, you almost feel like you’re carrying a single item. They don’t weigh too much either, so it takes little effort to move the boards from place to place.

Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is easy to set up and play straight from the box. The sturdy boards are made to last and the 8 included bean bags weigh 12 oz each, which is heavy enough to make them good for this type of game; less likely to slide past the opening and slide off of the board. The legs fold flat against the backside, so attaching the boards together with the Velcro is easy.

Cornhole is a popular backyard game and since I play it frequently when I go places, I decided it was time to get a game of my own. Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is a very good cornhole game set with a nice design and good durability. It’s a game I recommend for anyone who likes simple, outdoor entertainment for kids and guests.

I found myself envious of a colleague who had sunglasses with very good coverage, as I realized mine were a bit weak for this evil sun. I then realized a lot of the sunglasses I always thought of as gaudy may have just been that large because they were also trying to achieve the safety-glasses standard. Well, these achieve that safety-glasses standard without being too over the top. They look good, but still relatively nondescript. They provide good coverage from the sun as well, but they are also not too dark so if you need to continue to wear them inside for the safety protection, you don't look like you're trying too hard to be cool. These are very nice to have in those many situations where you occasionally need safety protection, but don't want to be swapping out safety glasses with sunglasses and then not knowing where to put the one you aren't currently using.

All that, and they also seem very good quality and come with a great case. I will go out of my way to really take care of these, because I know lots of polycarbonates can scratch (finely) easily. Not sure if these have any scratch-resistant properties, but no use taking any chances! Nice glasses!

text_fidelity_a: Helly-Hansen Brage Parka Okay, we haven't had any really cold weather here yet, but it's cooled off a lot. This is a very nice winter jacket and I'm looking forward to wearing it for yard work. I don't know about the 'woolish' hand feel, it seems like a normal polyester winter coat to me. It's very nice in that it's not bulky at all, but it was more than warm enough for the rainy, low 50'ish day I wore it. The drops of rain ran off, so it seems to repel a light rain/mist rather well (I wouldn't go out in a downpour with it, though), which gives me hope that this will help keep me dry in the snow. You have a big mesh 'inner pocket' which you can stick some gloves or a scarf or things in to help keep track of stuff, one small zipped inner pocket for glasses or maybe a small phone, and the external pockets are nice and deep. The jacket I received varies a little from the image here in that the hood is attached and doesn't look like the collar, so between it not quite being 'woolish' and that, the four stars, but over all it's a very nice winter parka that has a utilitarian look and I am confident that it'll be very warm and do a great job in the winter. Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android This RFLKT+ bike computer worked great with my iPhone 5, especially once I figured out how to use it! the instructions are bad - as in they have a small piece of paper in the box that tells you to scan the code to get to the instructions. I understand the reasoning - "technology changes fast and we want you to have the most up to date instructions." Okay, but sadly the instructions did not match the version of the device that I had, so I had to figure out some of it on my own. I mean you'd think they would keep the online instructions up to date if that's the reason they want you to go online to get them. I would have appreciated a brief "quick start" paper instruction inside the box.

Okay, enough about the instructions. Once I figured it out, this little device collected flawless from my iphone although you need to keep the app active or else the device shuts down. think of it as an extension of your iphone screen - a second monitor. I also have a Garmin heart rate monitor (ANT+) and a Garmin speed/cadence sensor (ANT+) on my bike. the Wahoo found both of those quickly and displayed the data accurately. I matched it against my Garmin 310XT watch and it matched up perfectly.

The one thing I had to remember was to start the app on the phone in order to get the distance and time to start recording! I was cruising along and watching my heart rate and cadence but couldn't figure out why the mileage wasn't getting logged until I realized I hadn't started things up on the iPhone. So this works well, and if you've already got other apps and like using your iphone then this is a great little device.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo RFLKT+ Bike Computer for iPhone & Android

text_fidelity_a:
WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump Every cyclist needs to carry a portable pump and an extra tube with them at all times. If you happen to get a flat ten miles away from your home, you are out of luck. You can't try to ride on a flat tire because it's dangerous and you'll ruin both the tire and the rim. It's a much better practice to have a high quality pump.

This Winningo portable pump is a perfect choice. The gauge takes out the guesswork and you can use this pump to get back to your regular tire pressure and continue with your ride. The valve can easily be converted between Presta and Schrader. The valve is attached to a rubber tube which makes inflation a lot more convenient. Many portable pumps attach directly to the valve stem, and if you're not careful you can accidentally snap off the stem when you inflate. The rubber tube makes that unfortunate outcome virtually impossible.

This portable pump is designed like a mini floor pump. It stands upright and a foot pedal flips out for stability. This allows you to pump up your tire with the assistance of body weight. You can easily inflate a tire to its recommended pressure with this pump, but the pump is compact enough to fit on a clip beside a water bottle cage on the downtube. This is a great product that will ensure you are well equipped to get back out on the road if you ever have a flat during a ride.
text_fidelity_b: WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump

YLG Oversized Comfort Bike Seat Comfortable Replacement Bike Saddle Memory Foam Soft Bike Saddle Waterproof Universal Fit Bicycle Seat for Women Men From the perspective of my rear end, this seat is great. It is very comfortable. It looks good and has great suspension. I actually worried the sides had too much give, but once I am on it, it is perfect)
I had a LOT of trouble finding a bike seat that didn't aggravate my sit bones. So this seat is a godsend.
However my thighs disagree a little. The angle of the sides of the seat gets too wide too fast compared to the nose. So it rubs the back of the thighs as you push the pedals down. text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary) I purchased the [[ASIN:B0018S4XIS Rayovac Sportsman LED Lantern (SE3DLNA)]] and this Coleman mini lantern. Both are bright but this pack away mini is great for when I need a little less light or want to carry a lantern that performs almost as well as the Rayovac but in a lot smaller package. For instance, this would be great to carry when walking outside in the dark because it's very light (about 8 ounces) and bright and makes a person visible enough to be seen.

What I like about this lantern is:
- It takes 4 AA batteries instead of the "highly in demand" D batteries that most flashlights use.
- The mini lantern fits in the palm of my hand when I collapse the LED portion into the unit.
- Mine came with a mini carabiner that I could hook onto the handle for easy carrying on a pant belt loop or backpack.
- The bottom battery compartment screws out by hand by turning the plastic grip several times until the cap came off.
- There are three modes of high, low, and strobe. The low mode does not look low to me and seems very similar to high but it's supposed to save battery life. Just pressing and releasing the top black button changes the mode.
- When the unit is collapsed, the light cannot accidentally be turned on which is a great feature.
- The unit is relatively light compared to full-sized lanterns.
- The package claims the LED lasts a lifetime and never has to be changed.

I purchased this at WallMart for $19.99 plus tax ($21.39) which is $1.60 less than Amazon's current price of $22.99.

This mini lantern suits me for small jobs and lights up my bathroom or kitchen with enough light to see without being blinding. In summary, there isn't anything I don't like about this lantern.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Pack Away LED Mini Lantern (Colors May Vary)

I researched a bit and there were no other promising brands on the market, so I went with these.

These weights are super high quality and should last for many, many years. They're also easy to adjust, weight wise. Each weight is actually comprised of 20 one-pound solid metal pellets that fit into little pouches.

So why only 3 stars? These 20lb weights have exactly the same velcro strap design as the smaller ones I have. When you're dealing with only 5lb per ankle, velcro works great. At 20lb, not so much.

These are difficult to put on and almost impossible to properly tighten. They need an entirely different strap design; something with a clasp or bracket and a friction strap, similar to a backpack, perhaps. Or...who knows. Just about anything would be better than this setup.

So here's the dilemma. There's nothing better on the market that I can find. These are workable but they're a total pain. If you need them you need them. But I feel like All Pro needs to step up and improve this design in a major way.

text_fidelity_a: Intech Golf Swing Impact Bag This impact bag measures 16 inches in diameter and 10 inches tall. It appears to be made of a very durable coated fabric that seems that it would stand up to a lot of use. It has a nylon strap-type handle on the top, under which lies the zipper that is used to install the towels or other soft materials that can be used to fill the bag for use. There is a plastic anchor loop on the bottom that could be used to anchor it to something solid to keep from having to consistently have to chase it after striking it. Now, I must admit that I am an intermediate golfer at best. With that, my main takeaways from using the bag is that it provides a durable, soft impact surface that can be used to swing a club and just practice the swing for purposes such as loosening up after injury, etc. While you could conceivably feel an open or closed club face at impact, I’m not that certain that there is a tremendous amount of actual feedback value that could be gained in reference to the swing. I certainly wouldn’t agree with the promo statement “Use at home to provide same quality practice time as hitting countless balls at the range”. There is also the issue of the noise. If used outside, especially in a fairly populated area, the loud noise that it makes at impact could certainly irritate neighbors. If used inside, I think you’d pretty much have to use earplugs. There may be other users that are more experienced golfers than I that might know of more valuable uses, but as for me, I’ll give it two stars.

SCHWINN Crewmaster Rower 100660, Gray We have a Schwinn recumbent bike that's held up well over the years, so were excited to try a Schwinn rower. This arrived well-packed in a series of boxes (be prepared to have a lot of packing materials to deal with), and it took about an hour to unpack and assemble, at least with two people. There's two main pieces that are heavy, and everything is included to put it together (other than something sharp to cut up the boxes, ties and packaging. There's a metal bar you need to remove from the front to put the 'stabilizer' in place, probably to keep anything from bending while in transit.
The motion is smooth once everything is together and the resistance is adjustable, which is good because you'll be able to use the equipment for a while.
You definitely need a pair of shoes while working out because of the position of the screws, and the screen/monitor is a little on the cheap side (it's powered by batteries and doesn't have a lot of options other than keeping track of your workout).
The long 'track' bar can bend upward to 'save' space or allow the machine to be moved about, but it still takes up a good bit of space and is heavy, so I don't think everyone will be able to move this about. But it is a good rowing machine and it does provide a great workout.
text_fidelity_b: SCHWINN Crewmaster Rower 100660, Gray

Kamagon Exercise Ball, Blue, 9-Inch with workout DVD This Kamagon ball gives me a fun and somewhat strenuous workout.

The ball is the perfect size and weight for me to handle.

It's the perfect weight because I adjusted it to the 4 pound level (by filling it with water) recommended for beginners. The side of the ball is clearly marked with weight line guides that indicate 4 through 12 pounds.

Kamagon is approximately the size of a basketball. The easy-grip handles on each side make it bigger. The handles are easy to grab during the exercises. This is important because, while the water inside the ball creates an instability that promotes a full core workout, the water seems to be sloshing in one direction while the ball is going in the other direction. No problem though with the big handles. What is interesting about this "destabilized weight" is that my awareness seems to be amplified during the workout. On the back of the Owner's Manual it says, "works the muscles while simultaneously training your nervous system." Yes, I can feel my brain working as my muscles and brain adjust to the movement of the water inside of the ball.

The DVD has two vigorous workouts. The Owner's Manual has workouts with clear black and white photos. There is also plenty of online support via the Kamagon website, facebook, and YouTube. There is a "Kamagon Workout Guide" included. You can eventually work up to five days a week with two days set aside for rest.

Be sure to read and follow the Owner's Manual before starting.

This ball had a strong odor when it first arrived -- I could smell it from across the room. I placed it outside overnight and now I can barely detect any smell at all.

I love this workout method that promotes balance, strength, aerobic endurance and neuromuscular coordination.

text_fidelity_a:
Stansport Survival Bottle Emergency First Aid Kit Sturdy cup with attached twist off lid. Stuffed inside is:
--ONE red medical bag with a variety of bandages, an empty zip lock bag, 4 alcohol wipes (fresh, plenty wet enough to wipe down fingers, phone, and keyboard), 2 sting relief pads, and a large triangular bandage. The little red medical bag has zipper closure, and has a mesh pocket on outside. This was hard to get out of the cup.
-- ONE mylar emergency blanket in zip lock bag. Also a challenge to wrangle out from cup
--ONE Pen light with clip, which needs 2 AAA batteries (non included)
--ONE Large, bright orange whistle that works with ease. Attached (cheap) carrying strap. One end has a working compass (it works, and is accurate. Mine anyway). One end can be twisted off to store smaller items. Nothing comes with it inside. I stuck my pinky finger in and didnt reach the end, so matches and such would be good.
-- ONE tea light. Appears to be a 4 hour (max) tea light.
--ONE basic but sturdy multi-tool in a black canvas sheath. Includes a key ring
-- ONE chemical body warmer. If it works, then it is a really nice addition. Can be used for pain, and can be used for added body warmth. I rely greatly on these warmers, and find them a must have for any emergency kit.
--ONE D-ring carabiner. Nice addition but it is super basic and cheap, really should have gone with something of more functional size. Dont rely on this. Anything would be better. Doesnt even work to hold the cup to a bag. Just too small, and will likely break.
--ONE fire starter stick
--and, ONE sturdy cup. Just a cup, will need to supply your own filtering if that is what you run up against. The twist cap has a reflective appearance. I can see myself, hence using this as a crappy mirror if needed. Not for vanity, but maybe I have something on my face or in my eye. Not sure if it would be enough for reflection in a signal, but its possible in a low key way.

If just using it for holding all this stuff, know that there is a little extra room for additional personalization. I'd add in a packet of pain reliever, an electrolyte powder (I buy tear off sticks for convenience), a nutrient dense snack- packet of peanut butter, maybe and a fruit/nut bar? water filtration tablets. Petroleum based chap stick. Possibilities are endless, so just think through a potential situation and work up from there. I want to be warm, dry, hydrated, and preferably fed, and be able to make some noise.

Overall a fair compilation. As with any survival gear, it comes down to the individual needs and ability to use said items. Also, there is so much variety out there, that pin pointing what to have or not to have is subjective. This gives a decent foundation of items. I'll put this in my car, or add to my every day carry bag. I personally like the addition of the chemical body warmer. That paired with the blanket will make all the difference in comfort. The whistle and compass (with additional storage) is the item I am most pleasantly surprised with. Some whistles take a lot of oomph to get sound, which isnt helpful if it is something you need in a dire situation. That and the compass is actually accurate and works quickly. I have purchased similar items and have had the compass not read correctly. No good if it isnt accurate! This is good. Penlight is nice addition. Just be sure to add batteries if you dont see any in your cup.

Minor differences from product picture and product description. The picture shows a pack of batteries, mine did not have any. The product description doesnt mention them at all (not even a reminder that we will need them). The fire starter stick is different, I think mine is better than what is shown in picture. Picture shows 2 body warmers, and product description says 1. My cup has 1.

As for getting everything back in once I got it out? Eh, with some finesse, yes.

4 stars. (could have been 5 if the product pictures, product description, and what I have in hand lined up- the differences may make or break someone buying choice. Again, overall I think it is a decent set that I got). $29 is reasonable price at time of review in 05/2022
text_fidelity_b: Stansport Survival Bottle Emergency First Aid Kit

text_fidelity_a:
UST TekFire Fuel-Free Lighter,orange If you want to get a fire going and you're using premade tinder or something homemade you're going to have to start small as the electrodes are rather close together. I was easily able to get small pieces of paper burning with little effort.
But to be honest? I burn a lot of Morning Star stick incense which fits perfectly between the electrodes of the TekFire. I got tired of grill/barbeque lighters with more safeties than some guns a few required two hands to operate or cheap lighters that even half full stop working after a few uses. I saw this rechargeable fuel-less lighter and have found i perfect for lighting my incense and tea lights as well as tall candles and oil lamps rather nicely. Durability is something we're going to have to see over time. The lighter comes with a two year warranty so there's plenty of time to give it a workout and see how it performs. So far? I'm very happy with this item.

Edit 10-06-2017 - This is sold as survival/camping gear. I simply use it around the house to light small candles and stick incense which small are a fairly tight fit between the electrodes. If this is meant for outdoor use why would they put a cheap, fragile and easily broken clear plastic hinge on the unit? Mine, after less than a month is severely wobbly. I would have no faith this would survive long term camping trips. I take care of my gear, as an example my backpack (a Jansport Eiger) is well over 30 years old. My sheath knife is similarly aged and even has my name and Explorer Post number scratched into the back of the sheath. I can't imagine this lighter lasting two years let alone 30+. I'm ready for the hinge to break any day now. I've dropped my review by one star due to poor quality/construction.

Osprey Orb Backpack I use a daypack for several purposes: (1) as the "personal item" most airlines allow besides a carry-on suitcase, (2) as a gym bag, and (3) for trips to amusement parks, hikes, or other vacation excursions. I consider this daypack the perfect size for these functions. I can carry a small pillow, a thermos, my Kindle, a snack, a sweatshirt, and a rain poncho inside it. Besides the main compartment, it has a small pocket that holds pens, lip balm and the like.

There is a nice selection of colors, and the straps are decently comfortable. I contacted the company that makes this product for the dimensions before buying, and the ones they gave me seem accurate: 18 in (46 cm) length/height x 11.5 in (29 cm) width x 8.5 in (22 cm) depth, with total dimensions of 38 inches.

By the way, here are examples of what airlines define as "personal items," and in my experience a daypack like this would have no problem meeting the standard for a personal item--you just can't have more than one of these personal items with you: camera in case, purse, briefcase, laptop in case, reading materials, umbrella, small "book-bag style" backpack. Technically the total dimensions of a personal item should not exceed 36 inches, but even since the airlines have been tightening up rules on carry-ons and personal items, I have never had any complaints about the size of my daypack, and sometimes I've carried one a bit larger than this one.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Orb Backpack

text_fidelity_a:
Miken 2014 REV-EX YRVX12 Baseball Bat (-12) For a full review please check out generationXdad

This will be my sons last year of playing machine pitch, next year we move up to kid pitch. Last year we used an aluminum baseball bat, it wasn't bad but I did notice that kids with composite bats seemed to be hitting the ball much further.

Composite bats have a high "trampoline effect," meaning that the ball comes off faster because of the material used in the bat. When a ball hits a traditional wood bat, it gets compressed before taking off, and loses energy in the process, so it comes out more slowly. In a metal or composite bat, the bat compresses instead, so the ball retains most of its energy and flies off at a higher speed.

Additionally, the carbon fiber of composite bats actually becomes more flexible with each hit. Their ability to compress goes up, and the balls fly off faster and faster.

So this year we decided to pick up a new composite bat for the season. After reading reviews and talking to a few parents we decided to go with the Miken Rev-Ex.
If you spend a little time looking at composite bats you’ll find there’s a lot of options out there that range in price from $150 to $300+. I definitely didn’t want to spend over $200 for a baseball bat. Miken came in at the price point I was looking for. We pulled the trigger and purchased the bat from Amazon (points, points, points)

Because of this you should check with the league your child plays in and make sure that composite bats are allowed. We play in Babe Ruth, composite bats are still allowed, however Little League only allows approved bats (This bat is on their approved list).

The first day my son started using the Miken Rev-Ex I noticed a difference in how far he could hit the ball. I would guess he added a solid 20 to 30 feet in distance to his solid hits. I also notice that balls hit in the infield were like bullets! Any solid hit off this bats comes off with speed!

So far my son has been very happy with the Miken Rev-Ex and has been taken extra care of it!

Final Review: For the price and performance I’m very happy with the improvements that I have seen. I can’t speak to warranty and hope that I never need to. If you’re looking for a good fairly priced composite bat then I recommend the Miken Rev-Ex.
Being an Amazon Prime member I had the bat in two days. First thing I noticed was the warning label on the bat.
text_fidelity_b: Miken 2014 REV-EX YRVX12 Baseball Bat (-12)
